title: Special application as practical use of the Word — Rome agrees faith must be efficacious
source_text: LXVI. Praeterea patet ex iis quae supra fuerunt dicta & exposita, Doctores Reformatos communi consensu docere proprium esse fidei salvificae & justificantis promissiones gratiae & salutis speciatim cuilibet credenti applicare, quam specialem applicationem Ecclesiae Romanae Doctores rejicere videntur. Sed primo quod attinet ad illos ex Reformatis qui applicationem istam in eo consistere volunt, quod fides viva atque justificans otiosa non sit & speculativa, sed quaecunque in Dei Verbo ipsi objiciuntur ad praxin & proprium credentis usum referat, manifestum est illos nihil hac in parte docere quod a Theologorum Ecclesiae Romanae doctrina abhorreat. Illi enim, ut supra visum est, ultro fatentur fidem, nisi efficax & actuosa sit, justificare & servare non posse.
pass_a_gloss: Furthermore it is clear from what was said and set out above that the Reformed Doctors by common consent teach that it is proper to saving and justifying faith to apply the promises of grace and salvation specially to each believer — which special application the Doctors of the Roman Church seem to reject. But first, as for those among the Reformed who want that application to consist in this, that living and justifying faith is not idle and speculative, but refers whatever is set before it in God Word to practice and the believer own use, it is manifest that they teach nothing in this part that is abhorrent from the doctrine of the theologians of the Roman Church. For those, as was seen above, freely confess that faith, unless it is efficacious and active, cannot justify and save.
pass_b_english: Reformed commonly teach special application of grace and salvation promises; Rome seems to reject it.
But if application means living faith is not idle speculation but turns the Word to practice and the believer use, Rome already grants faith must be efficacious and active to justify and save.
